findings.title: updateEvent fallback can never match, calendarId becomes undefined
findings.body: In updateEvent selectedCalendar is externalCalendarId when truthy else event.destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId). When the else branch runs externalCalendarId is falsy (null/undefined/''), so comparing stored externalIds to a falsy value never matches and the result is always undefined. Updates without an externalCalendarId therefore call Google with calendarId undefined instead of falling back to the destination calendar, causing update failures.

findings.title: deleteEvent fallback can never match, deletes from wrong calendar
findings.body: In deleteEvent calendarId uses the same pattern: externalCalendarId when truthy else find destination where externalId equals externalCalendarId. The else branch only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy so the find always returns undefined and the code falls back to 'primary'. A booking whose destination is a non-primary calendar but has no externalCalendarId will therefore delete from primary and leave the real event orphaned.

findings.title: createEvent patch ignores primary fallback
findings.body: createEvent inserts with calendarId selectedCalendar || 'primary' but the follow-up patch for hangoutLink uses raw selectedCalendar. When no destination matches credentialId, selectedCalendar is undefined, so insert goes to primary while patch is sent with undefined calendarId and fails, leaving the description without the hangout link.

findings.title: Google Meet fallback crashes when no destinationCalendar
findings.body: EventManager.create does const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [] then reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is null or empty the destructured value is undefined, so accessing .integration throws TypeError and crashes booking creation for Google Meet events without a destination calendar. It should be mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration.

findings.title: updateAllCalendarEvents reuses stale credential across references
findings.body: In updateAllCalendarEvents credential is declared outside the for loop and only reassigned when a lookup succeeds. If a reference has a credentialId that is found in neither memory nor DB, credential keeps the value from the previous iteration (or undefined on first). The code then calls updateEvent with the wrong credential, updating the wrong user's calendar and leaving the intended calendar stale, or throwing when undefined.

findings.title: Collective hosts dropped when organizer has no destinationCalendar
findings.body: handleNewBooking initializes evt.destinationCalendar to null when neither eventType nor organizer has one, then does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) for COLLECTIVE events. Optional chaining on null is a no-op, so second hosts' destinationCalendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are silently discarded and those hosts never get calendar events.

findings.title: CalDAV service ignores per-credential destination, only uses first host
findings.body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent takes only event and picks const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []. EventManager loops over every destination and passes credential/externalId, but this implementation ignores credentialId and always filters to the first destination. For collective bookings with multiple CalDAV/Lark/Office365 hosts this duplicates into the first host calendar and never creates in the others. Same limitation exists in Lark and Office365 services which also only read index 0.

findings.title: destinationCalendar changed from single object to array, breaking webhooks
findings.body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from DestinationCalendar|null to DestinationCalendar[]|null. Webhook payloads, emails and any external consumers expecting an object or null now receive an array. The e2e file shows the inconsistency: some triggers still expect null while BOOKING_REJECTED now expects [], proving the contract is both breaking and inconsistent across code paths that return null vs [].

findings.title: Calendar.createEvent now requires credentialId, breaking implementations
findings.body: The Calendar interface changed to createEvent(event, credentialId: number) with required second param, but Lark, Office365 and CalDAV implementations still declare createEvent(event) only. Callers passing only one arg get undefined credentialId at runtime, and third-party Calendar implementations will fail type-check. The param should be optional or all implementations updated.
